title: IVF vs ICSI and Gamete Micromanipulation
subject: ss-reproductive-medicine
refs: Gardner's Textbook of Assisted Reproductive Technologies 5e Ch 12 & 14
ESHRE Guideline on Good Practice in IVF Laboratories

steps.say: Assisted reproduction offers distinct methods for uniting male and female gametes. Standard insemination allows natural cellular selection across the cumulus mass. Micromanipulation bypasses all biological barriers.
steps.tx: In **conventional IVF**, an **insemination concentration** of 50000 to 100000 progressively motile morphologically normal spermatozoa is co-incubated per oocyte in microdrops. Conversely, intracytoplasmic sperm injection microinjects a single spermatozoon, with evidence-based **ICSI indications** restricted to severe male factor subfertility. Structured diagnostic algorithms and evidence-based reproductive protocols guide tailored clinical interventions across modern fertility management.

steps.say: Microinjection requires clear visualization of gamete maturation. Surrounding cumulus cells must be stripped away cleanly. Enzymatic digestion precedes mechanical pipetting.
steps.tx: Prior to microinjection, **cumulus denudation** is performed using hyaluronidase (80 IU/mL) for under 120 seconds combined with mechanical pipetting. Stripping the surrounding cumulus-corona radiata confirms an extruded first polar body, identifying mature metaphase II oocytes. Structured diagnostic algorithms and evidence-based reproductive protocols guide tailored clinical interventions across modern fertility management.

steps.say: Precise mechanical positioning prevents irreversible injury to maternal chromosomes. The second meiotic spindle lies directly adjacent to the extruded polar body. The microinjection needle must enter along an orthogonal axis.
steps.tx: During ICSI alignment, **polar body alignment** places the first polar body at 12 or 6 o'clock while the holding pipette secures the oocyte. The microinjection needle enters at the 3 o'clock **injection position**, safely avoiding disruption of the meiotic spindle apparatus. Structured diagnostic algorithms and evidence-based reproductive protocols guide tailored clinical interventions across modern fertility management.

steps.say: Sperm selection precedes aspiration into the injection needle. Immobilization ruptures the plasma membrane to initiate activation. Polyvinylpyrrolidone slows motility for precise handling.
steps.tx: Sperm selection occurs in viscous **polyvinylpyrrolidone**, where the embryologist performs flagellar **tail immobilization** with the pipette tip. Cracking the membrane induces **sperm immobilization**, permitting permeabilization and release of cytosolic factors required to initiate oocyte activation. Comprehensive clinical evaluation and disciplined reproductive management ensure optimal procedural outcomes and diagnostic precision across advanced subfertility protocols.

steps.say: Puncturing the egg membrane demands delicate tactile confirmation. The injection needle pushes the elastic surface until it yields. Aspiration of cytoplasm verifies True internal entry.
steps.tx: Advancement of the injection pipette through the zona pellucida produces prominent invagination of the oolemma. The embryologist applies gentle negative pressure to accomplish **oolemma aspiration**, verifying cytosolic breach via **membrane breakage** before depositing the spermatozoon. Comprehensive clinical evaluation and disciplined reproductive management ensure optimal procedural outcomes and diagnostic precision across advanced subfertility protocols.

steps.say: Egg activation depends upon a specialized sperm enzyme. Introductions of the male gamete release an active phospholipase into the egg. Intracellular calcium waves trigger resumption of meiosis.
steps.tx: Following microinjection, successful **oocyte activation** is triggered by the sperm-specific factor **phospholipase C zeta**. PLC-zeta hydrolyzes phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate to generate IP3, instigating oscillatory **calcium oscillations** that prompt cortical granule exocytosis and meiotic resumption. Comprehensive clinical evaluation and disciplined reproductive management ensure optimal procedural outcomes and diagnostic precision across advanced subfertility protocols.

steps.say: Fertilization assessment occurs at a fixed time point following microinjection. Normal fertilization is marked by two distinct pronuclei and two polar bodies. Atypical numbers signal genetic abnormalities.
steps.tx: At 16 to 18 hours post-insemination, normal fertilization is confirmed by the presence of **two pronuclei** and two polar bodies (**2PN 2PB**). Monopronuclear or multipronuclear zygotes reflect abnormal fertilization and are excluded from clinical culture. Structured diagnostic algorithms and evidence-based reproductive protocols guide tailored clinical interventions across modern fertility management.

steps.say: Total fertilization failure requires specialized rescue interventions in subsequent cycles. Lack of calcium release can be bypassed with artificial ionophores. Piezo assisted technology reduces physical deformation in fragile eggs.
steps.tx: Advanced micromanipulation techniques include **PICSI**, which utilizes **hyaluronic acid binding** to select mature spermatozoa with completed spermiogenesis. Furthermore, **IMSI** utilizes **high magnification** (over 6000x) to screen for subtle sperm **head vacuoles** before microinjection. Structured diagnostic algorithms and evidence-based reproductive protocols guide tailored clinical interventions across modern fertility management.
